_doc: Terrain painter (src/world/generation/terrain_painter.gd): the map generator's biome pass and the decoration pass. Biomes: every zone keeps its main biome (the profile's terrain) and gets 1-2 secondary biomes as noise-shaped patches that cover `coverage` of its tiles, drawn by `affinity` of the main biome (plus `patch_hint_weight` for each terrain the template profile lists under `patches`). Patch edges are dithered and smoothed so they look soft; zones joined by a pass bleed into each other for `gate_blend` tiles. Rivers (passable fords) cross a zone from wall to wall; lakes (deep water) never cut a zone apart, and `shores` turn some tiles around a lake into another biome. Zones of one template group share one plan, and rotate180 templates are painted point-symmetrically, so starts stay fair. `profiles` are keyed by map_templates.json profile id, `default` fills missing keys. Decoration: placed per tile from the biome's weighted `pool`, at the biome's `density`, thinned into clusters and clearings by value noise; no tile shares kind and variant with a neighbour. Kinds must exist in the decoration atlas (assets/manifest.json terrain.deco), so new scenery kinds plug in by adding them to pools.

decoration._doc: variants must match the atlas (assets/manifest.json terrain.deco.variants). cluster_cell is the noise lattice size in tiles; noise below `clearing` leaves a clearing. Towns keep `town_clearing` tiles free, other objects and heroes `object_margin`. With `border_mix`, a tile next to another biome may draw from that biome's pool, and with `grove` it repeats a neighbour's kind (in another variant) so groves form.

surfaces._doc: Cosmetic ground variants from the map scenery library (assets/map_scenery, category terrain), painted as noise patches over `coverage` of a terrain's open tiles. They never change the terrain or its rules; the map view draws them over the ground with feathered edges.

scenery._doc: Single-tile scenery pieces from the map scenery library (category decoration): one per `per_tiles` open tiles of a biome, at least `spacing` tiles apart, clear of roads and objects like decorations. Purely visual.

landmarks._doc: Large impassable set pieces from the map scenery library (category landmark), placed during terrain painting: each zone whose profile is listed gets one with `chance`, from the landmarks whose biome is its main biome (`any` biomes fit every zone), at most `max` per map and each landmark once (mirrored zones of rotate180 maps get a twin). The footprint becomes impassable ground and never cuts a zone apart.
